ai.definition: Advanced prosthetics are highly customized artificial limbs that incorporate advanced sensor technology and artificial intelligence to improve the user's mobility and functionality.
ai.howItWorks: AI algorithms process real-time patient data such as muscle signals, environmental conditions, and user preferences. This data is used to adjust the prosthetic in real time, optimizing its fit and function for improved performance and comfort.
ai.problemSolved: Traditional prosthetics often lack the ability to adapt to individual patients' needs and environments, leading to discomfort, reduced mobility, and decreased quality of life for amputees.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves 3D printing or custom casting of the prosthetic limb, followed by integration of sensors and AI components. This requires specialized equipment and expertise in both medical device design and advanced manufacturing techniques.
ai.buildProcess: The build process starts with a detailed patient assessment to determine the specific needs and requirements. Then, using CAD software, a customized design is created. Next, the prosthetic limb is manufactured through additive or subtractive manufacturing processes. Finally, sensors and AI components are integrated, followed by rigorous testing to ensure safety and functionality.
ai.costDrivers: High costs associated with advanced materials, specialized manufacturing equipment, and skilled labor. Additionally, ongoing development of AI algorithms adds significant expense.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as the technology continues to mature and gain acceptance in clinical settings. However, regulatory hurdles and high costs may slow widespread adoption initially.
ai.regulation: Regulated by medical device standards such as ISO 13485 for quality management systems and ISO 10993 for biocompatibility. Additionally, FDA approval or equivalent regional certifications are required before commercialization.
ai.risks: Technological risks include the complexity of integrating AI with prosthetics, potential software bugs, and the need for continuous updates. Clinical risks involve ensuring patient safety and addressing long-term health impacts. Financial risks stem from high initial costs and uncertain reimbursement models.
ai.profitability: Profitability is currently limited due to high development costs and low volume production. However, as the technology matures and gains market acceptance, profitability could improve with increased sales volumes and cost reductions through economies of scale.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include further integration of AI for predictive maintenance, enhanced sensor technologies for better feedback, and more advanced materials for improved durability and comfort.

subsystems.name: Socket and interface
subsystems.role: connects the prosthetic to the residual limb comfortably and securely.
parts: suspension system (suction, pin lock, or vacuum)

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: detects the user's intended movement and the limb's environment.

subsystems.name: Control system
subsystems.role: translates sensor signals into commands for the prosthetic joints.
parts: AI models trained on the user's signals

subsystems.name: Actuation
subsystems.role: moves powered joints such as elbows, wrists, and fingers.

subsystems.name: Power supply
subsystems.role: stores and manages energy for sensors, control, and motors.

subsystems.name: Structural frame
subsystems.role: carries loads and holds components in alignment.

buildSteps.title: Assess and scan the residual limb
buildSteps.detail: Clinicians measure length, circumference, and shape, often with 3D scanners, and record muscle signals to understand control sites.

buildSteps.title: Design the socket and limb
buildSteps.detail: CAD software is used to model a custom socket and select or design components based on the patient's needs and activity level.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate components
buildSteps.detail: The socket is 3D-printed or laminated from composites; frame parts are machined or moulded from carbon fibre and metals.

buildSteps.title: Integrate sensors and electronics
buildSteps.detail: EMG electrodes, IMUs, wiring, and connectors are embedded into the socket and limb, with care to avoid pressure points.

buildSteps.title: Program control algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Machine-learning models are trained on the user's muscle signals to classify intended movements, and parameters are set for safe operation.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and wire the limb
buildSteps.detail: Actuators, battery, control board, and sensors are fitted into the frame and connected, then the socket is attached.

buildSteps.title: Fit and tune
buildSteps.detail: The limb is tried on, alignment is adjusted, sensors are calibrated, and the user practices movements to refine control.

buildSteps.title: Iterate and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Follow-up visits adjust fit, update software, replace worn parts, and retrain algorithms as the user's condition changes.

prerequisites.why: carbon-fibre composites and titanium give strength without excessive weight.
EMG electrodes and inertial sensors are small enough to embed in a prosthetic.
low-power microcontrollers can run real-time control algorithms on the limb.
pattern recognition of muscle signals works in controlled settings but is not yet fully robust outside the clinic.
direct skeletal attachment is in clinical use but not widespread, and it could improve comfort and control.

pathway.milestone: commercially available microprocessor-controlled knees and myoelectric hands with basic pattern recognition
pathway.unlocks: improved mobility and function for many amputees.

pathway.milestone: AI control that adapts in real time to the user's intent, terrain, and load
pathway.unlocks: more natural, less mentally demanding walking and grasping.

pathway.milestone: osseointegrated implants with bidirectional neural interfaces
pathway.unlocks: direct neural control and sensory feedback, reducing reliance on surface electrodes.

pathway.milestone: fully integrated prostheses that feel and move like a natural limb
pathway.unlocks: seamless embodiment and everyday use without conscious effort.
